references.text: Describes the laws for the sin offering (חַטָּאת) that Aaron here performs for himself, including the slaughter of a young bull
During the consecration, Moses brought forward the sin offering bull, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head - the preparation for what Aaron now does independently
Moses' instruction to Aaron to take a calf for a sin offering, which Aaron now carries out in verse 8
On the Day of Atonement, Aaron was also to offer a sin offering bull for himself and his household
Aaron is to slaughter the sin offering bull that is for himself, parallel to the action in Lev 9:8
Instructions for the sin offering bull at priestly consecration, which form the basis for Aaron's action
The book of Hebrews explains that the high priest must offer sacrifices for his own sins, as Aaron does here
Contrasts the Levitical high priests who had to offer sacrifices for their own sins first, with Christ who did not need this
Mentions that the high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood for his own sins and those of the people
